claim: Brain function is mediated by the physiological coordination of a vast, intricately connected network of molecular and cellular components.
source: Brain function is mediated by the physiological coordination of a vast, intricately connected network of molecular and cellular components.
evidence: This is a general statement about brain function presented in the abstract without specific experimental data from this study, but draws on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The physiological properties of neural network components can be quantified with high throughput.
source: The physiological properties of neural network components can be quantified with high throughput.
evidence: This statement reflects established capabilities in neuroscience methodology.

claim: The ability to assess many animals per study has been critical in relating physiological properties to behavior.
source: The ability to assess many animals per study has been critical in relating physiological properties to behavior.
evidence: This reflects established practice in neuroscience research.

claim: The synaptic structure of neural circuits is presently quantifiable only with low throughput.
source: By contrast, the synaptic structure of neural circuits is presently quantifiable only with low throughput.
evidence: This statement describes the current state of the field that motivates the study.

claim: Low throughput of synaptic structure quantification hampers efforts to understand how variations in network structure relate to variations in behavior.
source: This low throughput hampers efforts to understand how variations in network structure relate to variations in behavior.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations imposed by low throughput methods.

claim: There is a methodological gulf between electron microscopic methods and light microscopic methods for neuroanatomical reconstruction.
source: For neuroanatomical reconstruction, there is a methodological gulf between electron microscopic (EM) methods, which yield dense connectomes at considerable expense and low throughput, and light microscopic (LM) methods, which provide molecular and cell-type specificity at high throughput but without synaptic resolution.
evidence: This describes the current state of available methods in the field.

claim: EM methods yield dense connectomes at considerable expense and low throughput.
source: For neuroanatomical reconstruction, there is a methodological gulf between electron microscopic (EM) methods, which yield dense connectomes at considerable expense and low throughput, and light microscopic (LM) methods, which provide molecular and cell-type specificity at high throughput but without synaptic resolution.
evidence: This characterizes the properties of EM methods based on established knowledge.

claim: LM methods provide molecular and cell-type specificity at high throughput but without synaptic resolution.
source: For neuroanatomical reconstruction, there is a methodological gulf between electron microscopic (EM) methods, which yield dense connectomes at considerable expense and low throughput, and light microscopic (LM) methods, which provide molecular and cell-type specificity at high throughput but without synaptic resolution.
evidence: This characterizes the properties of LM methods based on established knowledge.

claim: The authors developed a high-throughput analysis pipeline and imaging protocol using tissue expansion and light sheet microscopy (ExLLSM).
source: To bridge this gulf, we developed a high-throughput analysis pipeline and imaging protocol using tissue expansion and light sheet microscopy (ExLLSM) to rapidly reconstruct selected circuits across many animals with single-synapse resolution and molecular contrast.
evidence: This is a direct statement of what the authors developed in this study.

claim: ExLLSM can rapidly reconstruct selected circuits across many animals with single-synapse resolution and molecular contrast.
source: To bridge this gulf, we developed a high-throughput analysis pipeline and imaging protocol using tissue expansion and light sheet microscopy (ExLLSM) to rapidly reconstruct selected circuits across many animals with single-synapse resolution and molecular contrast.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the method developed, which is demonstrated throughout the manuscript.

claim: ExLLSM yields synaptic counts similar to those obtained by EM.
source: Using Drosophila to validate this approach, we demonstrate that it yields synaptic counts similar to those obtained by EM, enables synaptic connectivity to be compared across sex and experience, and can be used to correlate structural connectivity, functional connectivity, and behavior.
evidence: This is validated by experimental comparisons shown in Figure 3.

claim: ExLLSM enables synaptic connectivity to be compared across sex and experience.
source: Using Drosophila to validate this approach, we demonstrate that it yields synaptic counts similar to those obtained by EM, enables synaptic connectivity to be compared across sex and experience, and can be used to correlate structural connectivity, functional connectivity, and behavior.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the experiments comparing virgin and mated females (Figure 4H) and male-female differences (Figure 3M).

claim: ExLLSM can be used to correlate structural connectivity, functional connectivity, and behavior.
source: Using Drosophila to validate this approach, we demonstrate that it yields synaptic counts similar to those obtained by EM, enables synaptic connectivity to be compared across sex and experience, and can be used to correlate structural connectivity, functional connectivity, and behavior.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the pC2l-pIP10 experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: The ExLLSM approach fills a critical methodological gap in studying variability in the structure and function of neural circuits across individuals within and between species.
source: This approach fills a critical methodological gap in studying variability in the structure and function of neural circuits across individuals within and between species.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the demonstrated capabilities of the method.

claim: Major efforts are underway to reconstruct comprehensive wiring diagrams of the nervous systems of various species.
source: Major efforts are underway to reconstruct comprehensive wiring diagrams of the nervous systems of various species.
evidence: This describes the current state of the field, supported by citations to connectome projects.

claim: Connectome projects are fueled by recent advances in electron microscopy and automated image analysis methods.
source: These connectome projects are fueled by recent advances in electron microscopy (EM) and automated image analysis methods and motivated by the idea that knowing the exact pattern of synaptic connectivity within a neural network is necessary, though not sufficient, to understand how it functions.
evidence: This describes the technological basis of current connectome projects.

claim: Knowing the exact pattern of synaptic connectivity within a neural network is necessary, though not sufficient, to understand how it functions.
source: These connectome projects are fueled by recent advances in electron microscopy (EM) and automated image analysis methods and motivated by the idea that knowing the exact pattern of synaptic connectivity within a neural network is necessary, though not sufficient, to understand how it functions.
evidence: This is a conceptual statement about the relationship between structure and function in neuroscience.

claim: Most connectome projects are focused on generating reference connectivity maps for selected organisms.
source: Currently, most connectome projects are focused on generating reference connectivity maps for selected organisms (White et al., 1986; Ryan et al., 2016; Eichler et al., 2017; Hildebrand et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2018; Cook et al., 2019; Scheffer et al., 2020; Bae et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the current focus of connectome research, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The current state of connectomics research is analogous to the state of genomics research just over two decades ago.
source: This current state of connectomics research is somewhat analogous to the state of genomics research just over two decades ago.
evidence: This is an analogy drawn by the authors to contextualize the field.

claim: Advances in DNA sequencing made it possible to generate reference genomes for selected organisms.
source: Advances in DNA sequencing had made it possible to generate reference genomes for selected organisms, and ultimately also for humans.
evidence: This is a historical statement about genomics.

claim: The success of genome projects created the need to rapidly resequence targeted genomic regions across large numbers of samples.
source: The success of these genome projects created the need to rapidly resequence targeted genomic regions across large numbers of samples in order to determine how these sequences vary from individual to individual and from species to species, so as to better understand how the genome 'works' and how it evolves.
evidence: This describes the historical progression of genomics research.

claim: With the expanding collection of reference connectomes, there is an increasingly urgent need for methods that allow rapid but sparse reconstruction of neural circuits across large numbers of samples.
source: Similarly, with the expanding collection of reference connectomes, there is now an increasingly urgent need for methods that allow rapid but sparse reconstruction of neural circuits across large numbers of samples.
evidence: This is the motivation for the current study, drawn by analogy to genomics.

claim: Electron microscopy is not well suited to rapid reconstruction of neural circuits across large numbers of samples.
source: Electron microscopy, the method of choice for the reconstruction of dense reference connectomes, is not well suited to this task.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of EM for comparative studies.

claim: The time and cost involved in EM reconstruction currently limit comparative analyses to very small volumes.
source: The time and cost involved in EM reconstruction currently limit such comparative analyses to very small volumes (Bourne and Harris, 2012; Bumbarger et al., 2013; Valdes-Aleman et al., 2021) and to a few well-equipped laboratories (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes limitations of EM, supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: EM produces a dense image without molecular specificity.
source: Moreover, because EM produces a dense image without molecular specificity, it is exceedingly difficult to highlight individual neurons and molecules.
evidence: This describes a fundamental property of EM imaging.

claim: It is exceedingly difficult to highlight individual neurons and molecules in EM images.
source: Moreover, because EM produces a dense image without molecular specificity, it is exceedingly difficult to highlight individual neurons and molecules.
evidence: This is a consequence of EM's lack of molecular specificity.

claim: EM provides both too much and too little information for a typical comparative analysis of neuronal connectivity.
source: EM thus provides both too much and too little information for a typical comparative analysis of neuronal connectivity: too much, in that the specific neurons of interest first need to be identified amongst the vast tangle of processes revealed in the EM images, and too little, in that essential information on, for example, the chemical nature of individual connections is generally not available.
evidence: This is an evaluative statement about the suitability of EM for comparative studies.

claim: Light microscopy provides the means to readily highlight the neurons and molecules of interest across many individual animals.
source: Light microscopy (LM) provides the means to readily highlight the neurons and molecules of interest across many individual animals but has traditionally lacked the resolution needed to resolve individual synaptic connections (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes a key advantage of LM, illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Light microscopy has traditionally lacked the resolution needed to resolve individual synaptic connections.
source: Light microscopy (LM) provides the means to readily highlight the neurons and molecules of interest across many individual animals but has traditionally lacked the resolution needed to resolve individual synaptic connections (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes a traditional limitation of LM, illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: A combination of expansion microscopy and lattice light sheet imaging (ExLLSM) affords sufficient resolution to reveal single synapses and molecular labels.
source: Recently, however, a combination of expansion microscopy (Tillberg et al., 2016) and lattice light sheet imaging (Chen et al., 2014a) (ExLLSM) has been shown to afford sufficient resolution to reveal single synapses and molecular labels and to have sufficient speed to image large volumes of neural tissue across many animals (Gao et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the capabilities of ExLLSM, supported by citations.

claim: ExLLSM has sufficient speed to image large volumes of neural tissue across many animals.
source: Recently, however, a combination of expansion microscopy (Tillberg et al., 2016) and lattice light sheet imaging (Chen et al., 2014a) (ExLLSM) has been shown to afford sufficient resolution to reveal single synapses and molecular labels and to have sufficient speed to image large volumes of neural tissue across many animals (Gao et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the speed capabilities of ExLLSM, supported by citation.

claim: The authors aimed to develop a rapid, high-throughput and cost-effective ExLLSM pipeline to resample the connectivity of selected neural circuits with synaptic resolution and molecular and genetic specificity.
source: We aimed to develop a rapid, high-throughput and cost-effective ExLLSM pipeline to resample the connectivity of selected neural circuits with synaptic resolution and molecular and genetic specificity.
evidence: This is a statement of the study's aims.

claim: The primary goal was to establish a method to address variation in neural circuits.
source: Our primary goal was to establish a method to address variation in neural circuits.
evidence: This is a statement of the study's primary goal.

claim: Variations in structural connectivity arise through evolutionary, ontogenetic, environmental, stochastic, and experience-dependent processes.
source: Variations in structural connectivity arise through evolutionary, ontogenetic, environmental, stochastic, and experience-dependent processes.
evidence: This is a general statement about sources of variation in neural circuits.

claim: A major challenge in neuroscience is to understand how structural variations relate to species, sex, individual, and experiential differences in circuit physiology, function, and behavior.
source: A major challenge in neuroscience is to understand how such structural variations relate to species, sex, individual, and experiential differences in circuit physiology, function, and behavior.
evidence: This describes a key challenge in the field.

claim: There is not necessarily a one-to-one mapping between circuit connectivity, physiology, and output.
source: There is not necessarily a one-to-one mapping between circuit connectivity, physiology, and output (Marder, 2011; Marder et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a conceptual statement about circuit function, supported by citations.

claim: A full investigation of the structure–function relationships in neural circuits requires that each be examined across many individuals, ideally with structural and functional data acquired from the same samples.
source: Thus, a full investigation of the structure–function relationships in neural circuits requires that each be examined across many individuals, ideally with structural and functional data acquired from the same samples.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what is needed to understand structure-function relationships.

claim: ExLLSM should be well suited to examining structure-function relationships across many individuals.
source: ExLLSM should be well suited to this task.
evidence: This is a prediction about the suitability of ExLLSM for structure-function studies.

claim: The authors developed an ExLLSM circuit reconstruction method and pipeline to rapidly resample selected circuits within the Drosophila melanogaster connectome.
source: Here, we report the development of an ExLLSM circuit reconstruction method and pipeline, which we use to rapidly resample selected circuits within the Drosophila melanogaster connectome.
evidence: This is a statement of what was accomplished in the study.

claim: The ExLLSM method yields synaptic counts consistent with those obtained by EM.
source: We show that this method yields synaptic counts consistent with those obtained by EM, and that it can reveal structures such as electrical connections that are largely invisible to EM.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the L2, DA1-IPN, and SAG neuron experiments (Figure 3).

claim: ExLLSM can reveal structures such as electrical connections that are largely invisible to EM.
source: We show that this method yields synaptic counts consistent with those obtained by EM, and that it can reveal structures such as electrical connections that are largely invisible to EM.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the INX6 experiments (Figure 5).

claim: The ExLLSM pipeline can reveal state-dependent differences in neuronal connectivity.
source: Moreover, we apply our ExLLSM pipeline to reveal state-dependent differences in neuronal connectivity and correlate structural, physiological, and behavioral data across multiple individuals.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the virgin vs. mated female experiments (Figure 4H).

claim: The ExLLSM pipeline can correlate structural, physiological, and behavioral data across multiple individuals.
source: Moreover, we apply our ExLLSM pipeline to reveal state-dependent differences in neuronal connectivity and correlate structural, physiological, and behavioral data across multiple individuals.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the pC2l-pIP10 experiments (Figure 6).

claim: Drosophila brains were isometrically expanded to 8× their original size with high mechanical stability via an interpenetrating network gel.
source: Drosophila brains were dissected, in some cases from animals that had undergone prior behavioral and physiological analysis. Brains were isometrically expanded to 8× their original size with high mechanical stability via an interpenetrating network gel.
evidence: This describes the expansion protocol used in the study.

claim: No shrinkage or further expansion of samples was observed across multiple-day imaging sessions.
source: No shrinkage or further expansion of these samples was observed across multiple-day imaging sessions.
evidence: This is an observation about the stability of expanded samples.

claim: The central brain of Drosophila can be imaged in three colors in ~5 days at a resolution of ~30 × 30 × 100 nm.
source: With the LLSM settings used, the central brain of Drosophila can be imaged in three colors in ~5 days at a resolution (~30 × 30 × 100 nm) sufficient to identify individual electrical and chemical presynaptic and postsynaptic sites across the brain.
evidence: This describes the imaging capabilities achieved in the study.

claim: The resolution of ~30 × 30 × 100 nm is sufficient to identify individual electrical and chemical presynaptic and postsynaptic sites across the brain.
source: With the LLSM settings used, the central brain of Drosophila can be imaged in three colors in ~5 days at a resolution (~30 × 30 × 100 nm) sufficient to identify individual electrical and chemical presynaptic and postsynaptic sites across the brain.
evidence: This is demonstrated throughout the results section.

claim: The authors developed a largely automated pipeline to quantify synaptic connectivity between genetically identified neurons.
source: To process and analyze the images obtained by 8× ExLLSM (hereafter referred to as ExLLSM), we developed a largely automated pipeline to quantify synaptic connectivity between genetically identified neurons (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the computational pipeline developed, illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The pipeline combines a previously published automated image tile processing and stitching method with newly developed software.
source: The pipeline combines a previously published automated image tile processing and stitching method (Gao et al., 2019), with newly developed software to visualize multi-terabyte LM image volumes in 3D, semiautomatically (Figure 2B–G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and automatically segment neurons (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), detect and classify pre- and postsynaptic sites (Figure 2L–Q, Video 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 3), assign synaptic sites to segmented neurons, quantify the number, size, and location of neuronal connections (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), and to export these data as images and tables.
evidence: This describes the components of the analysis pipeline.

claim: The automatic presynaptic site segmentation achieved an average precision of 94% and recall of 88%.
source: The final synapse detection pipeline had an average precision of 94% and recall of 88% (Figure 2L-Q).
evidence: This is the performance evaluation of the synapse detection pipeline, shown in Figure 2Q.

claim: The automatic neuron segmentation achieved an average precision of 95% and recall of 79%.
source: On these crops, the average precision was 95% and average recall was 79% (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is the performance evaluation of the neuron segmentation pipeline, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2H.

claim: In Drosophila, presynaptic active zones are anatomically identified in EM images by T-bars.
source: In Drosophila, presynaptic active zones (hereafter referred to as presynaptic sites) are anatomically identified in EM images by T-bars (Huang et al., 2018; Buhmann et al., 2021), where synaptic vesicles are pooled and released.
evidence: This describes the EM correlate of presynaptic sites, supported by citations.

claim: Bruchpilot (Brp) protein is one component of T-bars.
source: One component of T-bars is the Bruchpilot (Brp) protein (Fouquet et al., 2009), which can be detected in LM images through either ubiquitous (Wagh et al., 2006) or genetically restricted labeling (Chen et al., 2014b).
evidence: This describes the molecular composition of T-bars, supported by citations.

claim: BRP can be detected in LM images through either ubiquitous or genetically restricted labeling.
source: One component of T-bars is the Bruchpilot (Brp) protein (Fouquet et al., 2009), which can be detected in LM images through either ubiquitous (Wagh et al., 2006) or genetically restricted labeling (Chen et al., 2014b).
evidence: This describes labeling strategies for BRP, supported by citations.

claim: In an EM volume comprising seven optic lobe columns from one animal, an average of 207 presynaptic sites were detected per L2 neuron.
source: In an EM volume comprising seven optic lobe columns from one animal obtained by focused-ion beam milling scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM), an average of 207 presynaptic sites were detected per L2 neuron (Takemura et al., 2015).
evidence: This is data from a published EM study, cited for comparison.

claim: Using ubiquitous BRP labeling, ExLLSM counted an average of 210 presynaptic sites per L2 neuron across 30 neurons.
source: We imaged large sections of the optic lobe medulla and segmented 10 individual L2 neurons in each of three flies, counting an average of 210 presynaptic sites per L2 neuron (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Using genetically restricted BRP labeling (STaR), ExLLSM counted an average of 195 synapses across 30 L2 neurons.
source: With this method, we counted an average of 195 synapses, also across a total of 30 L2 neurons (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: L2 synapse counts obtained by 8× ExLLSM were similar with both labeling methods and matched the EM counts.
source: Thus, the L2 synapse counts obtained by 8× ExLLSM were similar with both labeling methods and matched the EM counts (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the ExLLSM and EM data, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: DA1-IPN neurons comprise a group of 7–8 sexually dimorphic neurons that relay conspecific odors from the DA1 glomerulus in the antennal lobe to the mushroom body and lateral horn.
source: The DA1-IPN neurons comprise a group of 7–8 sexually dimorphic neurons that relay conspecific odors from the DA1 glomerulus in the antennal lobe to the mushroom body and lateral horn (Marin et al., 2002; Wong et al., 2002; Stockinger et al., 2005; Jefferis et al., 2007; Kurtovic et al., 2007; Kohl et al., 2013; Figure 3K–P).
evidence: This describes the DA1-IPN neurons, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The female ExLLSM presynaptic site count for DA1-IPN neurons (2251) was similar to both EM datasets (FIB-SEM hemibrain: 2274; TEM: 1837 left, 1735 right).
source: On average, the female ExLLSM presynaptic site count of 2251 was similar to both EM datasets (FIB-SEM hemibrain: 2274; TEM: 1837 left, 1735 right) (Figure 3M).
evidence: This is a comparison of ExLLSM and EM data, shown in Figure 3M.

claim: The average DA1-IPN presynaptic site count in males (2466) was higher than in females (2251), but this difference was not statistically significant.
source: Although the average count in males (2466) was higher than in females, this difference was not statistically significant (t-test, two-tailed p=0.25).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of male and female data.

claim: The bilaterally paired female-specific SAG ascending neurons relay the fly's mating status (virgin or mated) to the central brain.
source: The bilaterally paired female-specific SAG ascending neurons relay the fly's mating status (virgin or mated) to the central brain (Feng et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the function of SAG neurons, supported by citation.

claim: In 18 females, ExLLSM counted an average of 1440 SAG presynaptic sites.
source: In 18 females, we labeled SAG via a LexAGAD driver line, segmented the SAG neurons from the off-target neurons, and counted an average of 1440 presynaptic sites (Figure 3Q–S, Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 3S.

claim: In the FIB-SEM female hemibrain, the SAG neurons have 1198 presynaptic sites.
source: In the FIB-SEM female hemibrain (Scheffer et al., 2020), the SAG neurons have 1198 presynaptic sites, which falls within the range of counts we obtained by ExLLSM (Figure 3S).
evidence: This is data from a published EM study, cited for comparison and shown in Figure 3S.

claim: Most Drosophila synapses are polyadic.
source: Most Drosophila synapses are polyadic (Scheffer et al., 2020), such that a single presynaptic site has multiple postsynaptic contacts.
evidence: This describes a property of Drosophila synapses, supported by citation.

claim: In the FIB-SEM hemibrain dataset, the two SAG neurons make 5534 connections to downstream neurons from 1198 presynaptic sites.
source: In the FIB-SEM hemibrain dataset, the two SAG neurons make 5534 connections to downstream neurons from 1198 presynaptic sites.
evidence: This is data from the FIB-SEM hemibrain used for comparison.

claim: Of the SAG connections in the FIB-SEM hemibrain, 938 are made to pC1 neurons via 677 SAG presynaptic sites.
source: Of these connections, 938 are made to pC1 neurons via 677 SAG presynaptic sites.
evidence: This is data from the FIB-SEM hemibrain used for comparison.

claim: There is no known postsynaptic analog to BRP that labels all or most postsynaptic sites in Drosophila.
source: Although ExLLSM is in principle compatible with any primary antibody, there is no known postsynaptic analog to BRP that labels all or most postsynaptic sites in Drosophila.
evidence: This describes a limitation in available molecular markers.

claim: The current ExLLSM protocol is limited to three-color imaging.
source: In particular, our current ExLLSM protocol is limited to three-color imaging, which makes it challenging to simultaneously visualize two cell types and two molecular markers.
evidence: This describes a technical limitation of the current protocol.

claim: Using the Drep2 labeling approach, ExLLSM counted an average of 729 SAG to pC1 connections made by an average of 583 presynaptic sites (n = 11).
source: Using this approach (Figure 4B–F, Video 3), we counted an average of 729 SAG to pC1 connections made by an average of 583 presynaptic sites (n = 11) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Both SAG>pC1 connection averages from ExLLSM are slightly lower than the counts obtained from the single FIB-SEM hemibrain sample (938 and 677, respectively), but the EM counts fall within the range obtained by ExLLSM.
source: Both averages are slightly lower than the counts obtained from the single FIB-SEM hemibrain sample (938 and 677, respectively), but we note that the counts for this EM sample fall within the range we obtained by ExLLSM (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a comparison of ExLLSM and EM data, shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Using the membrane contact approach to quantify SAG>pC1 connectivity, ExLLSM obtained an average of 501 connections (n = 6).
source: Using the second approach to quantify connectivity, which quantifies the number of SAG presynaptic sites that contact the pC1 membrane (Figure 4I–O, Video 4), we obtain an average of 501 connections (n = 6) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The membrane contact method may more consistently undercount synapses compared to the postsynaptic marker method.
source: The most connections we counted in a single sample was 604, below the count of 677 in the EM sample, suggesting that this method may more consistently undercount synapses.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the maximum ExLLSM count to the EM count.

claim: Without specific postsynaptic labeling, fine neural processes may be missed more often using ExLLSM than EM due to discontinuities inherent in immunohistochemistry and 8× expansion methods.
source: Postsynaptic sites are often located in fine neural processes (Schneider-Mizell et al., 2016; Scheffer et al., 2020), and without specific labeling using a postsynaptic marker such as Drep2, these fine processes may be missed more often using ExLLSM than EM due to the discontinuities inherent in the immunohistochemistry and 8× expansion methods.
evidence: This is an explanation for why the membrane contact method may undercount, supported by citations.

claim: ExLLSM reconstruction strategies result in similar connection counts that are in general agreement with those obtained by EM.
source: We conclude that the ExLLSM reconstruction strategies used here result in similar connection counts that are in general agreement with those obtained by EM.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison experiments.

claim: The authors recommend the use of a specific postsynaptic marker where practical to avoid undercounting.
source: We recommend the use of a specific postsynaptic marker where practical to avoid undercounting.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the comparison of methods.

claim: All approaches to counting synapses, including EM, rely on detection methods that generally have high specificity but lower sensitivity, and therefore all undercount connections to various degrees.
source: Nonetheless, we note that all of these approaches, including EM (Scheffer et al., 2020), rely on detection methods that generally have high specificity but lower sensitivity, and therefore all undercount connections to various degrees.
evidence: This is a general statement about limitations of synapse detection methods, supported by citation.

claim: Relative synaptic counts are usually more informative than absolute numbers.
source: For practical purposes, however, relative synaptic counts are usually more informative than absolute numbers, and so a slight but consistent undercounting is not necessarily problematic.
evidence: This is a conceptual statement about the interpretation of synapse counts.

claim: ExLLSM enables a much larger number of samples to be surveyed than EM, providing a more accurate assessment of relative connectivity.
source: ExLLSM further mitigates this concern because it enables a much larger number of samples to be surveyed than EM, providing a significantly more accurate assessment of relative connectivity regardless of which labeling strategy is used.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the advantages of ExLLSM for comparative studies.

claim: The pC1 neurons regulate female receptivity and egg-laying.
source: The pC1 neurons regulate female receptivity and egg-laying (Wang et al., 2020a; Wang et al., 2020b), both of which change dramatically after mating.
evidence: This describes the function of pC1 neurons, supported by citations.

claim: Female receptivity and egg-laying change dramatically after mating.
source: The pC1 neurons regulate female receptivity and egg-laying (Wang et al., 2020a; Wang et al., 2020b), both of which change dramatically after mating.
evidence: This is a statement about behavioral changes after mating.

claim: After mating, sensory neurons in the uterus detect the presence of a male seminal fluid protein.
source: After mating, sensory neurons in the uterus detect the presence of a male seminal fluid protein (Häsemeyer et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2009), and the SAG neurons relay this signal from the uterus to pC1 neurons in the brain (Feng et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the sensory pathway for detecting mating, supported by citations.

claim: SAG neurons relay the mating signal from the uterus to pC1 neurons in the brain.
source: After mating, sensory neurons in the uterus detect the presence of a male seminal fluid protein (Häsemeyer et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2009), and the SAG neurons relay this signal from the uterus to pC1 neurons in the brain (Feng et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the role of SAG neurons, supported by citation.

claim: Both SAG and pC1 neurons have higher basal activity in virgin females than in mated females.
source: Both the SAG and pC1 neurons have higher basal activity in virgin females than in mated females (Feng et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2020a), and so we hypothesized that they may also have more synaptic connections in virgin females than in mated females.
evidence: This describes the physiological state of these neurons, supported by citations.

claim: The authors hypothesized that SAG and pC1 neurons may have more synaptic connections in virgin females than in mated females.
source: Both the SAG and pC1 neurons have higher basal activity in virgin females than in mated females (Feng et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2020a), and so we hypothesized that they may also have more synaptic connections in virgin females than in mated females.
evidence: This is a hypothesis tested in the study.

claim: The average number of SAG presynaptic sites was similar in mated and virgin females.
source: The average number of SAG presynaptic sites was similar in mated and virgin females (Figure 4H , t-test, two-tailed p=0.26) but 25% fewer of these presynaptic sites were connected to pC1 in mated females, resulting in 28% fewer connections (Figure 4H, t-test, two-tailed p=0.03 and 0.02, respectively).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 4H.

claim: 25% fewer SAG presynaptic sites were connected to pC1 in mated females compared to virgin females.
source: The average number of SAG presynaptic sites was similar in mated and virgin females (Figure 4H , t-test, two-tailed p=0.26) but 25% fewer of these presynaptic sites were connected to pC1 in mated females, resulting in 28% fewer connections (Figure 4H, t-test, two-tailed p=0.03 and 0.02, respectively).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Mated females have 28% fewer SAG>pC1 connections compared to virgin females.
source: The average number of SAG presynaptic sites was similar in mated and virgin females (Figure 4H , t-test, two-tailed p=0.26) but 25% fewer of these presynaptic sites were connected to pC1 in mated females, resulting in 28% fewer connections (Figure 4H, t-test, two-tailed p=0.03 and 0.02, respectively).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 4H.

claim: SAG>pC1 synapses are remodeled after mating.
source: These data establish that SAG>pC1 synapses are indeed remodeled after mating and, moreover, demonstrate the power of ExLLSM to reveal and quantify state-dependent changes in neuronal connectivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the virgin vs. mated comparison data.

claim: ExLLSM can reveal and quantify state-dependent changes in neuronal connectivity.
source: These data establish that SAG>pC1 synapses are indeed remodeled after mating and, moreover, demonstrate the power of ExLLSM to reveal and quantify state-dependent changes in neuronal connectivity.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the virgin vs. mated comparison.

claim: Neurons communicate through electrical connections called gap junctions.
source: Neurons also communicate through electrical connections called gap junctions (Güiza et al., 2018; Nagy et al., 2018), which are difficult to detect in EM images.
evidence: This is a general statement about gap junctions, supported by citations.

claim: Gap junctions are difficult to detect in EM images.
source: Neurons also communicate through electrical connections called gap junctions (Güiza et al., 2018; Nagy et al., 2018), which are difficult to detect in EM images.
evidence: This describes a limitation of EM, supported by citations.

claim: Invertebrate gap junction channels are formed by innexin proteins.
source: Invertebrate gap junction channels are formed by innexin proteins (Syrjanen et al., 2021), which provide a molecular label to visualize and quantify electrical connections using ExLLSM.
evidence: This describes the molecular composition of gap junctions, supported by citation.

claim: Innexin proteins provide a molecular label to visualize and quantify electrical connections using ExLLSM.
source: Invertebrate gap junction channels are formed by innexin proteins (Syrjanen et al., 2021), which provide a molecular label to visualize and quantify electrical connections using ExLLSM.
evidence: This is a capability demonstrated in the study (Figure 5).

claim: Functional gap junctions are generally composed of two hemichannels, one from each neuron.
source: Functional gap junctions are generally composed of two hemichannels, one from each neuron.
evidence: This is a general statement about gap junction structure.

claim: Antibody staining against gap junction proteins reveals both distributed punctate signals and pronounced aggregations.
source: Antibody staining against gap junction proteins reveals both distributed punctate signals and pronounced aggregations (Phelan et al., 2008; Markert et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the appearance of gap junction protein staining, supported by citations.

claim: Punctate signals may label hemichannels, which themselves may be functional channels.
source: Punctate signals may label hemichannels, which themselves may be functional channels (Skerrett and Williams, 2017), whereas aggregations plausibly label gap junctions composed of two hemichannels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the staining patterns, supported by citation.

claim: There are eight types of innexin proteins in Drosophila.
source: In Drosophila, there are eight types of innexin proteins (Stebbings et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a factual statement about Drosophila innexins, supported by citation.

claim: INX6 immunoreactivity was most pronounced in the fan-shaped body.
source: As previously reported (Wu et al., 2011; Troup et al., 2018; Ammer et al., 2022), INX6 immunoreactivity was most pronounced in the fan-shaped body (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, consistent with previous reports and shown in Figure 5A-D.

claim: In expanded tissue, the fan-shaped body INX6 aggregations were revealed to be composed of distinct clusters of INX6.
source: In expanded tissue, the fan-shaped body INX6 aggregations were revealed to be composed of distinct clusters of INX6 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, shown in Figure 5C.

claim: INX6 clusters generally resembled the clusters of pre- and postsynaptic proteins found at chemical synapses.
source: These INX6 clusters generally resembled the clusters of pre- and postsynaptic proteins found at chemical synapses (Figures 2—4) and could be automatically classified as possible gap junctions using the same workflows used to detect chemical synapses (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: This is an observation about the similarity of INX6 clusters to synaptic protein clusters.

claim: INX6 clusters could be automatically classified as possible gap junctions using the same workflows used to detect chemical synapses.
source: These INX6 clusters generally resembled the clusters of pre- and postsynaptic proteins found at chemical synapses (Figures 2—4) and could be automatically classified as possible gap junctions using the same workflows used to detect chemical synapses (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: This demonstrates the versatility of the synapse detection pipeline, shown in Figure 5B-D.

claim: Gap junctions essential for memory formation are formed between DPM and APL neurons in the mushroom body.
source: We also visualized INX6 immunoreactivity in the mushroom body, where gap junctions essential for memory formation are formed between DPM and APL neurons (Wu et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the functional significance of DPM-APL gap junctions, supported by citation.

claim: INX6 immunoreactivity was weak and punctate in the mushroom body, with few if any clusters.
source: Using ExLLSM, we found that INX6 immunoreactivity was weak and punctate in the mushroom body, with few if any clusters (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: Punctate INX6 signals colocalized with DPM and APL neurons.
source: These punctate signals colocalized with DPM and APL neurons (Figure 5E-H).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, shown in Figure 5E-H.

claim: DPM-associated INX6 contacted APL membranes and APL-associated INX6 contacted DPM membranes.
source: We found that DPM-associated INX6 contacted APL membranes and APL-associated INX6 contacted DPM membranes, but did not detect any contact between INX6 in DPM and INX6 in APL.
evidence: This is an observation from the study about the localization of INX6.

claim: No contact was detected between INX6 in DPM and INX6 in APL.
source: We found that DPM-associated INX6 contacted APL membranes and APL-associated INX6 contacted DPM membranes, but did not detect any contact between INX6 in DPM and INX6 in APL.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: Electrical coupling between DPM and APL neurons is mediated by heterotypic gap junctions composed of INX6 and INX7, respectively.
source: Previous findings indicate that electrical coupling between DPM and APL neurons is mediated by heterotypic gap junctions composed of INX6 and INX7, respectively (Wu et al., 2011), which suggest that we may be visualizing part of the gap junctions formed between these neurons.
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular composition of DPM-APL gap junctions, supported by citation.

claim: The ExLLSM pipeline can detect electrical as well as chemical connections.
source: Although additional work is necessary to characterize the structure of hemichannels and homo- and heterotypic gap junctions in superresolution LM, these data demonstrate the ability of our ExLLSM pipeline to detect electrical as well as chemical connections.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the INX6 experiments (Figure 5).

claim: ExLLSM has the potential to greatly accelerate the quantification of electrical connectivity between neurons using the suite of antibodies to label all eight Drosophila innexins.
source: Using the recently developed suite of antibodies to label all eight Drosophila innexins (Ammer et al., 2022), ExLLSM has the potential to greatly accelerate the quantification of electrical connectivity between neurons and extend correlative structure–function studies to electrical as well as chemical connections.
evidence: This is a prediction about future applications of ExLLSM, based on the availability of new reagents.

claim: The male courtship song consists of a series of loud pulses, interspersed with bouts of continuous humming known as the sine song.
source: The male courtship song consists of a series of loud pulses, interspersed with bouts of continuous humming known as the sine song (Greenspan and Ferveur, 2000; Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This describes the structure of Drosophila courtship song, supported by citation and shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: pC2l neurons respond to both auditory and visual cues.
source: The pC2l neurons respond to both auditory and visual cues (Kohatsu and Yamamoto, 2015; Deutsch et al., 2019), and activating a subset of these neurons elicits pulse song acutely, followed by sine song post-activation (Deutsch et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the sensory responses of pC2l neurons, supported by citations.

claim: Activating a subset of pC2l neurons elicits pulse song acutely, followed by sine song post-activation.
source: The pC2l neurons respond to both auditory and visual cues (Kohatsu and Yamamoto, 2015; Deutsch et al., 2019), and activating a subset of these neurons elicits pulse song acutely, followed by sine song post-activation (Deutsch et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the behavioral effect of pC2l activation, supported by citation.

claim: Using a different genetic driver line that labels eight pC2l neurons in each hemisphere, pC2l activation produced acute courtship song in most flies with natural pulse and sine characteristics.
source: Here, using a different genetic driver line that labels eight pC2l neurons in each hemisphere, we found that pC2l activation produced acute courtship song in most flies with natural pulse and sine characteristics (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is experimental data from the study, shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: pIP10 cells are bilaterally paired male-specific descending neurons.
source: pIP10 cells are bilaterally paired male-specific descending neurons.
evidence: This describes the identity of pIP10 neurons.

claim: pIP10 activity is necessary and sufficient for the production of pulse song and, to a lesser extent, sine song.
source: pIP10 activity is necessary and sufficient for the production of pulse song and, to a lesser extent, sine song, and influences song choice during courtship (von Philipsborn et al., 2011; Clemens et al., 2018; Calhoun et al., 2019; Ding et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the function of pIP10 neurons, supported by citations.

claim: pIP10 activity influences song choice during courtship.
source: pIP10 activity is necessary and sufficient for the production of pulse song and, to a lesser extent, sine song, and influences song choice during courtship (von Philipsborn et al., 2011; Clemens et al., 2018; Calhoun et al., 2019; Ding et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the function of pIP10 neurons, supported by citations.

claim: pC2l cells are presynaptic to pIP10, with an average of 92 pC2l>pIP10 connections per brain.
source: We established that pC2l cells are presynaptic to pIP10, counting an average of 92 pC2l>pIP10 connections per brain.
evidence: This is experimental data from the study.

claim: There was a strong linear relationship between the number of synaptic contacts and the strength of the functional connection between pC2l and pIP10 cells across animals (Pearson's r = 0.88, p=0.009).
source: There was a strong linear relationship between the number of synaptic contacts and the strength of the functional connection between pC2l and pIP10 cells across animals (Pearson's r = 0.88, p=0.009, Figure 6G).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the correlation between structural and functional connectivity, shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Structural connectivity between pC2l and pIP10 was less strongly correlated with optogenetically elicited song (Pearson's r = 0.67, p=0.09).
source: Structural connectivity between pC2l and pIP10 was less strongly correlated with optogenetically elicited song (Pearson's r = 0.67, p=0.09, Figure 6H), and least of all with naturally stimulated song (Pearson's r = 0.49, p=0.27, Figure 6H).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the correlation between structural connectivity and behavior, shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Structural connectivity between pC2l and pIP10 was least correlated with naturally stimulated song (Pearson's r = 0.49, p=0.27).
source: Structural connectivity between pC2l and pIP10 was less strongly correlated with optogenetically elicited song (Pearson's r = 0.67, p=0.09, Figure 6H), and least of all with naturally stimulated song (Pearson's r = 0.49, p=0.27, Figure 6H).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the correlation between structural connectivity and behavior, shown in Figure 6H.

claim: There was a strong linear correlation between the functional connection and optogenetic song (Pearson's r = 0.83, p=0.02).
source: We also observed a strong linear correlation between the functional connection and optogenetic song (Pearson's r = 0.83, p=0.02, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), more so than between structural connectivity and optogenetic song (Pearson's r = 0.67, p=0.09, Figure 6G) and between functional connectivity and naturally stimulated song (Pearson's r = 0.37, p=0.41, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: There was no correlation between the baseline fluorescence of the GCaMP signal and the structural connection (Pearson's r = −0.09, p=0.85).
source: These relationships are unlikely to merely reflect individual variations in expression levels of the GCaMP6 reporter as there was no correlation between the baseline fluorescence of the GCaMP signal and the structural connection (Pearson's r = −0.09, p=0.85, Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a control analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: pC2l and pIP10 directly drive the pulse component of courtship song, with only indirect contributions to sine song production.
source: Previous evidence suggests that pC2l and pIP10 directly drive the pulse component of courtship song, with only indirect contributions to sine song production (Deutsch et al., 2019; Ding et al., 2019; Roemschied et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about the function of these neurons, supported by citations.

claim: Structural connectivity was more strongly correlated with optogenetic pulse song production (Pearson's r = 0.75, p=0.054) than total song (Pearson's r = 0.67, p=0.09) or sine production alone (Pearson's r = 0.11, p=0.82).
source: Indeed, separating song into its pulse and sine components revealed that structural connectivity was more strongly correlated with optogenetic pulse song production (Pearson's r = 0.75, p=0.054, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C) than total song (Pearson's r = 0.67, p=0.09, Figure 6H) or sine production alone (Pearson's r = 0.11, p=0.82, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis shown in Figure 6H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ExLLSM allows a variable feature of behavior to be correlated with individual differences in structural connectivity.
source: These data demonstrate that ExLLSM allows a variable feature of behavior to be correlated with individual differences in structural connectivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pC2l-pIP10 experiments.

claim: The protocols developed allow a single sample to be prepared and analyzed within a week.
source: The protocols we have developed allow a single sample to be prepared and analyzed within a week and can be readily multiplexed to process several samples in parallel.
evidence: This describes the throughput of the method.

claim: The ExLLSM protocols can be readily multiplexed to process several samples in parallel.
source: The protocols we have developed allow a single sample to be prepared and analyzed within a week and can be readily multiplexed to process several samples in parallel.
evidence: This describes the scalability of the method.

claim: Other light sheet microscopes can be utilized to image large volumes of 8× expanded samples.
source: Although LLSM provides an excellent combination of imaging resolution and speed with limited photobleaching (Gao et al., 2019), other light sheet microscopes can also be utilized to image large volumes of 8× expanded samples.
evidence: This is a statement about the generalizability of the approach.

claim: The ExLLSM method relies on relatively affordable microscopy and computational resources that are widely available.
source: As such, our method relies on relatively affordable microscopy and computational resources that are widely available, bringing connectomics research within reach of smaller labs.
evidence: This is a statement about the accessibility of the method.

claim: The ExLLSM approach brings connectomics research within reach of smaller labs.
source: As such, our method relies on relatively affordable microscopy and computational resources that are widely available, bringing connectomics research within reach of smaller labs.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the impact of the method on the field.

claim: The software tools developed are freely available and have been designed with efficiency and flexibility in mind.
source: These tools are freely available (Lillvis et al., 2021) and have been designed with efficiency and flexibility in mind.
evidence: This describes the availability and design of the software tools.

claim: The ExLLSM tools should be well suited for any organism in which neurons can be reliably labeled and tissue can be sufficiently expanded.
source: Accordingly, these tools should be well suited for any organism in which neurons can be reliably labeled and tissue can be sufficiently expanded.
evidence: This is a prediction about the applicability of the tools to other organisms.

claim: ExLLSM is applicable to other Drosophila species, nematodes, rodents, zebrafish, and organoids.
source: This includes other Drosophila species, nematodes, rodents, zebrafish, and organoids, for each of which genetic tools to label specific neurons are available and expansion microscopy protocols have been established (Freifeld et al., 2017; Gao et al., 2019; Yu et al., 2020; Rodriguez-Gatica et al., 2022).
evidence: This lists organisms for which the method should be applicable, supported by citations.

claim: With the development of neuron labeling methods that leave fewer gaps in the fluorescent signals of expanded samples, automated single-neuron segmentation should become feasible.
source: With the development of neuron labeling methods that leave fewer gaps in the fluorescent signals of expanded samples, automated single-neuron segmentation should become feasible (Januszewski et al., 2018), allowing connectivity to be assessed at the level of single cells rather than single-cell types, as we have done here.
evidence: This is a prediction about future improvements to the method.

claim: Improved labeling methods would allow connectivity to be assessed at the level of single cells rather than single-cell types.
source: With the development of neuron labeling methods that leave fewer gaps in the fluorescent signals of expanded samples, automated single-neuron segmentation should become feasible (Januszewski et al., 2018), allowing connectivity to be assessed at the level of single cells rather than single-cell types, as we have done here.
evidence: This is a prediction about future capabilities.

claim: Improved labeling methods would likely allow more densely labeled neurons to be traced, ultimately perhaps even entire connectomes.
source: Such methods would likely also allow more densely labeled neurons to be traced, ultimately perhaps even entire connectomes (Gao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a prediction about future capabilities, supported by citation.

claim: A further improvement would come through the generation of reagents to visualize specific components of chemical and electrical synapses in a cell-type-restricted manner.
source: A further improvement would come through the generation of reagents to visualize specific components of chemical and electrical synapses, ideally in the form of genetic tools that label endogenous molecules in a cell-type-restricted manner (Chen et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is a prediction about future improvements, supported by citation.

claim: Probes that reveal the functional state as well as the location of synaptic molecules would be particularly valuable for ExLLSM.
source: Because ExLLSM enables correlative structural and functional studies, probes that reveal the functional state as well as the location of such molecules would be particularly valuable.
evidence: This is a prediction about valuable future developments.

claim: Comparative ExLLSM can be used to reveal state-dependent differences in neuronal connectivity.
source: We have shown here that comparative ExLLSM can be used to reveal state-dependent differences in neuronal connectivity.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the virgin vs. mated experiments.

claim: The ExLLSM method is ideally suited to explore how genetic, environmental, and stochastic processes work together to create individual differences in neuronal connectivity.
source: More generally, the method is ideally suited to explore how genetic, environmental, and stochastic processes work together to create individual differences in neuronal connectivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the potential applications of the method.

claim: In combination with new methods to genetically identify and label homologous neurons across species, ExLLSM will enable new studies on circuit and behavior evolution.
source: In combination with new methods to genetically identify and label homologous neurons across species (Stern et al., 2017; Tanaka et al., 2017; Seeholzer et al., 2018; Ding et al., 2019; Auer et al., 2020), this approach will also enable new studies on circuit and behavior evolution.
evidence: This is a prediction about future applications, supported by citations.

claim: By facilitating the collection of both functional and structural data from the same samples, the ExLLSM pipeline allows individual and species differences in circuit structure to be correlated with differences in neurophysiology and behavior.
source: By facilitating the collection of both functional and structural data from the same samples, our ExLLSM pipeline also allows individual and species differences in circuit structure to be correlated with differences in neurophysiology and behavior.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the pC2l-pIP10 experiments.

claim: The ExLLSM approach to neural circuit reconstruction fills a critical methodological gap in exploring the links between genes, structure, physiology, and behavior.
source: Our ExLLSM approach to neural circuit reconstruction thereby fills a critical methodological gap in exploring the links between genes, structure, physiology, and behavior, and should be a powerful tool in efforts to understand how connectomes work and how they evolve.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the significance of the method.

claim: ExLLSM should be a powerful tool in efforts to understand how connectomes work and how they evolve.
source: Our ExLLSM approach to neural circuit reconstruction thereby fills a critical methodological gap in exploring the links between genes, structure, physiology, and behavior, and should be a powerful tool in efforts to understand how connectomes work and how they evolve.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the potential impact of the method.
